subject: Digital Logic

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Boolean Algebra
questions.text: Convert $(345.625)_{10}$ into Binary, Octal, and Hexadecimal. Perform subtraction using 2's complement: $(25)_{10} - (42)_{10}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Boolean Algebra
questions.text: State and prove De Morgan's Theorems. Realize basic gates (AND, OR, NOT) using only Universal Gates (NAND / NOR).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Boolean Algebra
questions.text: Simplify Boolean function $F(A,B,C,D) = \sum m(0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15) + d(1, 4)$ using Karnaugh Map (K-Map). Realize the minimal SOP expression using NAND gates.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Boolean Algebra
questions.text: Simplify the Boolean function using Quine-McCluskey (Tabulation) Method: $F(w,x,y,z) = \sum m(1, 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15)$. List all Prime Implicants and Essential Prime Implicants.
Design a Half Adder and Full Adder circuit using logic gates. Design a 4-bit Parallel Binary Adder/Subtractor circuit using 7483 IC and XOR gates.
Design a 3-to-8 line Decoder with enable input using basic gates. Implement full subtractor using 3-to-8 decoder and external OR gates.
Design an 8-to-1 Multiplexer (MUX) using logic gates. Implement Boolean function $F(A,B,C,D) = \sum m(1, 3, 4, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15)$ using an 8-to-1 MUX.
Design a BCD to Seven-Segment Display Decoder for a common cathode display.

Differentiate between Combinational Logic and Sequential Logic circuits. Differentiate between Latches and Flip-Flops. Explain Clocked SR Flip-Flop with characteristic table, characteristic equation, and race-around condition.
Explain Master-Slave JK Flip-Flop with logic diagram and timing waveforms. Show how Master-Slave configuration eliminates the race-around problem.
Explain Flip-Flop Conversion: Convert a JK Flip-Flop into a D Flip-Flop and a T Flip-Flop by designing conversion logic with excitation tables.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Registers, Counters and Memory Devices
questions.text: Design a 3-bit Synchronous Up/Down Counter using JK Flip-Flops with state diagram, excitation table, K-maps, and circuit diagram.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Registers, Counters and Memory Devices
questions.text: Design a Mod-10 (Decade) Asynchronous/Ripple Counter using T or JK flip-flops.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Registers, Counters and Memory Devices
questions.text: Explain 4-bit Shift Registers: Serial-In Serial-Out (SISO), Serial-In Parallel-Out (SIPO), Parallel-In Serial-Out (PISO), and Universal Shift Register with bidirectional control.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Registers, Counters and Memory Devices
questions.text: Explain Programmable Logic Devices (PLD): Compare PROM, PLA (Programmable Logic Array), and PAL (Programmable Array Logic). Implement Boolean functions using PLA.
